title: Interview candidate: Elixir of Progress (@elucidating.extradimensional.space), who answered questions about 5D golf, agent swarms and how they want to post
summary: Elixir of Progress (2,288 followers) wrote 456 posts in the window. The post that travelled furthest was a long thread about the FAA outage (15 Nov, 1,780 likes), which the digest flags and which is not on this card; the digest's "Breakout" line and six of the eight question-and-answer pairs it stores for this account come from that thread and the arguments around it. Outside it: on 13 Nov they answered a member's question about how they think about golf in five dimensions; on 13 and 14 Nov they put two small pages on their own site, built with a model's agent swarm, and replied to people who noticed; on 15 Nov they answered a member's open question about how they would like their own posting to change. The card lists 9 of their replies with the post each one answered.

candidate.source: The digest's Interview material (sections.interview), third of five. One of the four pairs the digest prints is on this card (the question about power); the other three sit in flagged stories.

checks.optOutList: not on the opt-out list (packages/scraper/config/optout.json, loaded through the tool)
checks.bio: not checked: the digest carries no bios and research has no network. The scraper reports that it excluded accounts with profile opt-outs before the digest was written.
checks.windowPosts: Read their 95 top-level posts and all of their replies to other people's questions that the data holds (33, of which 10 are in flagged stories or carry a sensitivity mark). The week is dominated by the outage thread and what followed it: arguments, blocks, and posts about politics. There are also posts about their child and a post that begins "At the risk of leaking my identity". None of that is on the card. No post asks not to be quoted; one post says they have a tool to find people screenshotting them.

didInWindow: Put a page on their own site styled after a favourite device (13 Nov, charting.extradimensional.space), and a second page, the "bsky far-frame observatory", which shows images posted by accounts near you and how popular they are (14 Nov, charting.extradimensional.space/rpla/, 24 likes, with an image). They said both were made with a Gemini model's swarm feature in a short time. Wrote a blog post (18 Nov) that they describe as election related; it is not on the card.
couldBeShown: The two pages on charting.extradimensional.space are public links. The researcher has not opened them. The observatory post has an image with no alt text in the data.
4D Golf is a published game; the "5d-levels" and "5d-golf" answers describe playing its five-dimensional levels.

posts.text: example?

Unlike a lot of swarm tools that maintain a sort of persistent state, Agy's swarm stuff works well even for smaller tasks. It's unusual in that way ime.

It's consistent, it doesn't burn a ton of tokens, it scales really well, and it's as happy to run for 3 minutes as it is for many hours.
That does seem pretty trivial. But then why do they need so much power?
Lots of customers. Also training. Training bursts load, and this is sort of maximally bad for the grid we have in America.
Is there some point where we’ve mostly finished training?

No. Probably never.

The things, even with transformers aside deep learning is sort of The Everything Sauce.
Yeah 4d golf was great. I still haven't beaten any of the 5d levels though. They promised a VR version that hasn't come yet, which is a bummer.

The 5d levels are incredible and worth setting aside time for.

For me the saddest thing is no proper multiplayer.
how do you think about golf in 5D, personally

Well, in a more structured way. I think 4d is just sort of barely within cognitive reach of a human mind that lives and breathes it. You can start to get intuition. But 5d just breaks it, and it breaks your intuition about 4d too because you can rotate your perspective around 2 new axis.

When I played the 5D levels I used a lot more of the game's "lock to hole" tooling and such, and I played several test rounds drawing sketch maps of the topology of each dimension. I found this helped, because one of the holes has 2 paths to take.
posts.role: answer, continued (same author, next post in the same reply chain)

posts.text: Another hole has an elaborate looping (in the 5th and 4th) spiral and this only became apparent when I started trying to draw slice maps.

This might just be the level design tho.

Replied to the "usage" answer. The digest marks this account as shown in the previous episode.

notUnderstood: I do not know the device the first page is styled after ("the Sony Jackal 300") and have not seen either page. "Agy" is the Antigravity coding tool and "Hydrogen" a Gemini model, as far as the posts show. I have not played 4D Golf.
leftOut: Everything in or about the outage thread, including three of the four pairs the digest prints and the "Breakout" post. A question from a member about a blog post on Ghost (the post is about an election). A question about a story they told that begins "At the risk of leaking my identity". Replies in arguments about whether computers make mistakes. A post about their child's homework (minors). Posts about blocking and about a tool that lists people who block them. An opening joke about a public figure's affairs.
sensitive: The thing this account was known for in the window is out of bounds: the outage thread is flagged in the digest (story 18 per the scope review), and the politics around it runs through the week. A portrait made from the pairs here would leave out what they mostly posted about. The "power" and "training" pairs are about electricity demand, which is near a contested policy subject though not partisan as asked and answered; the first mentions "the grid we have in America". The anime thread around the "anime-title" pair has remarks about "incels" by both people; the pair itself is only a title. Two prompts are from accounts that were in the previous episode. They said in a post on 16 Nov that they run a tool to find people screenshotting them, which a reviewer may read as a wish not to be clipped (R11); I could not tell.
